why: Fresh app (int 37ba577, isolated root, userData r1-S6-critic), 03:06Z, load 2.1. `python3 -m http.server 47302` in the vibepet repo gave the chip ':47302 Directory listing for /'. Node servers titled 'Vite + React + TS' in the vibepet repo (:47353) and the delta repo (:47354) gave two identical chips. ports.js had project=vibepet/delta for each of them. The snapshot sends only {port,pid,name,http}, with name = the page title, so the repo is lost and no chip names a session. Nothing maps a listener to a session: it has a cwd only, with no pid ancestry, so a session's own server can never be linked to its row. With 5–15 sessions, generic titles make servers impossible to tell apart. The variant where the session starts its own background server was not re-run (it needs paid turns, and spend was at the stop). It goes through the same code path.
cause: main.js:372 (name: s.title || ports.label(s); no session/repo field reaches the chip); ports.js:162-170 (server rows carry only cwd/project; no listener→session mapping)

why: 03:06Z. Node listen(47381,'localhost') bound [::1]:47381 only (lsof). http://localhost:47381 returned 200 'Vite + React + TS' (node and curl). 127.0.0.1:47381 was ECONNREFUSED. The chip read ':47381 node (vibepet)' with Open disabled. Shared port: node on *:47351 ('Delta dashboard', delta repo) plus page.py on 127.0.0.1:47351 ('Vibepet status', vibepet repo) gave two identical chips, ':47351 Vibepet status'. Open on each chip (pids 103 and 115) requested http://localhost:47351, and that reached 'Delta dashboard' via node and curl, so the 127.0.0.1 server can't be opened from the pet. HTTPS on 127.0.0.1:47383 answers https with 200 and plain http with ECONNRESET. Its chip read ':47383 node (vibepet)' with Open disabled. Vite's default host binds ::1 on this Mac, so this hits the most common dev server.
cause: ports.js:81 (probe is always http://127.0.0.1; ignores the listener host kept at ports.js:30 and TLS); main.js:428 + main.js:397 (Open is always http://localhost:<port>, enabled only if that probe answered)

why: 03:06:33Z. slow.js on *:47385 in the vibepet repo makes every request wait until 20 s after start. The chip first appeared 7.5 s after listen as ':47385 node (vibepet)' with Open disabled. Samples every 4 s up to 59.6 s after listen (4+ refreshes) were unchanged, while http://localhost:47385 and 127.0.0.1:47385 both returned 200 'Next.js app'. ⋯ → Localhost → ':47385 node (vibepet) · 1m' → 'Open http://localhost:47385' was enabled:false. The first probe's 800 ms timeout is cached as http:false for the life of the pid:port. A Next.js dev server's compile-on-first-request routinely takes longer than 800 ms.
cause: ports.js:168 with ports.js:153 (one probe per pid:port, cached; dropped only when the listener goes, ports.js:172); ports.js:79-86 (800 ms timeout → {http:false}); main.js:372 + main.js:397 (http !== false gates Open in Home and the menu)

why: Fresh app. Servers (node and python, delta/atlas repos) started and stopped at random moments with U(0,12 s) gaps, n=14 valid trials. Run a (03:12Z) had 4 valid trials; 6 were voided because Home was no longer open (chip never rendered), a harness artifact. Run b (03:25–03:31Z) had 10. Listen → chip: median 11.8 s (4.0–14.6 s). Exit → chip gone: median 10.8 s (3.0–14.7 s). Main's ports cache refreshed every 12.0 s (median of n=68, 11.9–12.06 s). load1 1.1–3.3, no sleep. The 'tick' carrying each change matched the DOM within 50 ms. The rubric anchor is ≤3 s (≤6 s for 85), so the median is about 4× that. The stale window also feeds r1-S6-09.
cause: ports.js:181-182 (poll(minMs = 10e3): a refresh starts only on a tick ≥10 s after the last one); main.js:381-382 (watchLocal reads the cache each 3 s tick, so a refresh lands one tick later; TICK_MS at main.js:20)

why: 03:33:58Z. Z (:47443, delta repo) was killed right after a refresh. 310 ms after its exit, its chip was still listed with Open enabled. ✕ asked 'Stop node (delta) on :47443?' why: No fleet session had a running background task during my window. atlas's bfldnuko5 was interrupted around 03:03Z, before my menu capture at 03:10Z, which listed only ended tasks. Creating a new one needs paid turns, and spend was at the stop. So I reproduced it on the real data instead of the UI. The vibepet fleet transcript (Claude Code 2.1.287) records the running task as 'Command running in background with ID: bhl322btn.', and '(ID: bhl322btn)' appears nowhere. I ran the app's own ports.taskInfo on that transcript cut before the task-notification, which is what the app read while the task ran. It returns {status:null, desc:null, summary:null}, so listTasks names the task 'bhl322btn' and the menu shows '● bhl322btn · vibepet'. On the full transcript it resolves to 'Start HTTP server on port 47120', the tool_use description, which was present from the start. The UI was not re-shot.
cause: ports.js:98 (running-task match expects '(ID: <id>)'; the only other match needs the end-of-task notification); ports.js:137 (name falls back to the raw id); main.js:406
